label: ari:C.5.1
statement:
\begin{proposition}[the equianharmonic point is neither an extremum]\label{ari:C.3.2}


Set $T_0=\sqrt3/2$, $\mu_0=(2-\rho)/3$, and
$p=\wp'_\rho(\mu_0)$. Then $p\ne0$, $p^2=-g_3(\rho)$, and, for
$\delta=\tau-\rho$ on the order-three root chart,
\begin{align*}
 \mu&=\frac{2-\tau}{3}
      +\frac{3p}{16\pi^2}\delta^2
      +\frac{3ip}{32\pi^2T_0}\delta^3+O(\delta^4),\\
 t&=\frac{ip^2}{\pi^3}\delta^3
        \left(1+\frac{3i}{2T_0}\delta+O(\delta^2)\right),\\
 \log N&=\tfrac14\log3+\frac7{192}\operatorname{Re}t
       -\frac{9\pi}{512T_0|p|^{2/3}}|t|^{4/3}
       +O(|t|^{5/3}).
\end{align*}
Thus
\[
 D_{\rm part}(t)=-\frac3{2\pi}\log48
       +\frac7{32\pi}\operatorname{Re}t
       -\frac{27}{256T_0|p|^{2/3}}|t|^{4/3}
       +O(|t|^{5/3}).
\]
The point $t=0$ is neither a local maximum nor a local minimum.
\end{proposition}


\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.,leftmargin=*]
\item We rederive the differentiation in Proposition~\ref{push:src:D.4.4}: put
$\ell=\partial_z\log\vartheta_1(\mu,\tau)$,
$a=\operatorname{Im}\mu/T$, $Z=\ell+2\pi ia$, and
$R=\mu'-a$. The theta heat equation and
$\wp=-\partial_z\ell-E$ give on the zero locus
\[
 \mu'=\frac{i\ell}{2\pi}-\frac{ig_2}{6\pi\wp'},\qquad
 R=\frac{iZ}{2\pi}-\frac{ig_2}{6\pi\wp'},\qquad
 \partial_\tau\log N=\frac{Z}{8\pi i}(Z+4\pi iR).
\]
These equations give the factored formula of Proposition~\ref{push:src:D.4.4}
with its stated normalizations. At $\rho$ the unit endomorphism fixing the
nonzero order-three point forces the gradient of $U_\rho$ there to
vanish, so $Z=0$. Explicitly the unit $\rho-1$ fixes $\mu_0$ modulo
the lattice and has no fixed nonzero real covector. Hence
$a=\mu'=-1/3$ and $\ell=2\pi i/3$.

\item Along the zero locus, a further heat-equation differentiation gives
\[
 \ell'=\frac{i\wp'}{4\pi}+\frac{iEg_2}{6\pi\wp'}.
\]
The Ramanujan derivatives at $\rho$ are
\[
 g_2'=\frac{3ip^2}{\pi},\quad
 g_2''=\frac{5i}{T_0}g_2',\quad
 \frac{(\wp')'}{\wp'}=\frac{3i}{2T_0},\quad E=\frac\pi{T_0}.
\]
They give $\mu''=3p/(8\pi^2)$,
$\mu'''=9ip/(16\pi^2T_0)$ and hence the asserted $\mu$ expansion.
Expansion of $t=g_2^3/(g_2^3-27g_3^2)$ gives the displayed $t$
formula. Since $\partial_\tau a=R/(2iT)$, one has
\[
 Z=\frac{ip}{4\pi}\delta+O(|\delta|^2),\qquad
 R=\frac{3p}{8\pi^2}\delta+O(|\delta|^2).
\]
The derivative formula now gives the harmonic cubic
$\operatorname{Re}(7ip^2\delta^3/(192\pi^3))=(7/192)
\operatorname{Re}t+O(|\delta|^4)$.

\item For the next term, direct differentiation of the Gaussian gives
\[
 \partial_\tau\partial_{\bar\tau}\log N
       =-\frac\pi{2T}|R|^2
       =-\frac{9|p|^2}{128\pi^3T_0}|\delta|^2+O(|\delta|^3).
\]
After the harmonic cubic has been written as a function of $t$, the
order-three stabilizer permits only a radial term in degree four:
in the linearizing coordinate
$(\tau-\rho)/(\tau-\bar\rho)$ invariant monomials have exponents
whose difference is divisible by three. The coefficient of
$|\delta|^4$ is therefore $-9|p|^2/(512\pi^3T_0)$, since
$\partial_\delta\partial_{\bar\delta}|\delta|^4=4|\delta|^2$.
Converting $|\delta|^4$ to $|t|^{4/3}$ proves the expansion, including
the remainder. Its nonzero linear term in $\operatorname{Re}t$
has both signs, which proves the last assertion. In particular
superharmonicity at this root point does not make it a local maximum.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}



\subsection{CM and torsion}
\begin{cited}[no smooth CM-torsion parameter]\label{ari:C.5.1}


There is no $t\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0,1\}$ for which $E_t$ has
complex multiplication and $P_t$ is torsion. On the smooth models
at $t=0,1$ after base change of orders $3,4$, respectively, the
limiting points have orders $3,2$. Thus these are the only CM
torsion points on the completed family.
\end{cited}
The expanded source derivation is retained in the proof compendium, Paper~I, label \nolinkurl{ari:C.5.1}.




This applies \citet[Theorem~4.15]{BourdonClarkStankewicz2017} and \citet[Theorem~20.12 and Corollary~20.13]{Sutherland2023CM}; the exact finite enumeration is retained. A complete re-derivation is given in \CompendiumRef{I}{app:rederive:ari-C.5.1}.



\section{Global heights and the eleven rational CM fibres}

We use the equation
\[
 E_t:Y^2=X^3-\frac34t^3(t-1)X+\frac14t^4(t-1)^2,
 \qquad P_t=(0,t^2(t-1)/2).
\]
Its discriminant is $27t^8(t-1)^3$. Our canonical height is
$\widehat h_O(P)=\frac12\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-2}h(x(nP))$.
In particular the bilinear Mordell--Weil self-pairing used in the
supplied surface calculation is $2\widehat h_O$.
For a finite place $v$ above the rational prime $p$, we normalize
$|p|_v=p^{-1}$ and set $n_v=[K_v:\Q_p]$. At an archimedean
place $n_v$ is one or two, according as the place is real or complex.

\begin{proposition}[the global formula]\label{ari:C.6.1}


For every number field $K$, every $t\in K\setminus\{0,1\}$,
and the section just specified,
\begin{equation}\label{ari:eq:ch-global}
 \sum_{\sigma:K\hookrightarrow\C}\log N(P_{\sigma(t)})
 =\sum_{v\nmid\infty}n_v\lambda_v(P_t)
          -[K:\Q]\widehat h_O(P_t).
\end{equation}
Here the local heights are invariant under change of Weierstrass
model and satisfy, when $nP\ne O$,
\begin{equation}\label{ari:eq:ch-local-mult}
 \lambda_v(nP)=n^2\lambda_v(P)-\log|\psi_n(P)|_v
                   +\frac{n^2-1}{12}\log|\Delta|_v.
\end{equation}
At a complex embedding $\lambda_v(P)=-\log N(P)$; complex
embeddings are counted separately in \eqref{ari:eq:ch-global}.
For rational $t$, put $A_t=\exp(\sum_p\lambda_p(P_t))$.
Then $A_t$ is a positive real algebraic number and
\[
 N(P_t)=A_t e^{-\widehat h_O(P_t)},\qquad
 D_{\rm part}(t)=\frac6\pi
       \left(\log\frac{A_t}{2\sqrt3}-\widehat h_O(P_t)\right).
\]
Thus $N(P_t)$ is algebraic if and only if
$e^{\widehat h_O(P_t)}$ is algebraic.
\end{proposition}

label: night:P2.2
cdp:st:E15
statement:
\begin{proposition}[Tangent cohomology and Kuranishi germs of positive combs]\label{cdp:st:E15}


For each positive-comb manifold $X_m$ constructed in
\cite{Viaclovsky2026Combs}, in particular for every $m\geq12$ in
its stated construction, one has
\[
 h^\bullet(X_m,T_{X_m})=(2m+1,\,8m+1,\,6m+1,\,0).
\]
Its Kuranishi germ is smooth and reduced of dimension $8m+1$.
A locally miniversal family is supplied by all sufficiently nearby
admissible period sections on the root curve, with the affine
attachment classes fixed. Its members have algebraic dimension one
and torus fibrations with the same three critical values,
multiplicities $3,4$, and hexagonal fibre type.
\end{proposition}

label: maps:src:D.2.11
statement:
\begin{theorem}[all orders $3k$ for $IV^*+II+I_2$]\label{maps:src:D.2.11}



The rational elliptic surface
\[
 y^2=x^3-3t^3(t-1)x+t^4(t-1)(2t-1),
 \qquad P=(t^2,t^2),
 \tag{D.C1}\label{maps:eq:D.C1}
\]
has fibres $IV^*,II,I_2$ at $0,1,\infty$ and Mordell--Weil group
$\mathbb Z$ generated by $P$. Put $M=\mathcal O(P-O)$ and
$Q=3P$. Let $C_0$ be the identity component of the $I_2$ fibre.
There is a linearization with divisor $C_0$, and its torus
family has Yang's index-one Type C marking. Keep the type-$II$
filling unchanged and use the index-one toroidal filling at
$I_2$. At $IV^*$ choose any logarithmic order and invariant vector
\[
 m=3k,\qquad v=n(\gamma-u-w)+r\delta,
 \qquad k>0,\quad n,r\in\mathbb Z,
 \quad\gcd(n,3k)=1.
\]
The resulting compact smooth complex threefold has
\[
 \pi_1(X)=\mathbb Z/|n|,\qquad
 H_i(X;\mathbb Z)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathbb Z&i=0,6,\\
 \mathbb Z/|n|&1\leq i\leq4,\\
 0&i=5.
 \end{cases}
\]
Consequently $n=\pm1$ gives the standard $S^6$ for every positive
$k$. This is an affirmative unbounded configuration for
Viaclovsky's Question 4. The linearization is supported on one
$I_2$ component, so the local-narrowness restriction of the public
engine does not include this input.
\end{theorem}

label: maps:src:D.2.24
statement:
\begin{theorem}[both $I_3^*$ profiles are excluded from the natural sphere table]\label{maps:src:D.2.24}



Neither OS profile $46$ nor $46/II$ can give a homotopy six-sphere
in the natural section-line construction and local filling sector
of \ref{maps:src:D.2.22}, for any admissible logarithmic orders or affine twists.
This includes arbitrary choices of original and semistable logarithmic
fillings at $I_3^*$.
\end{theorem}

label: maps:src:D.2.27
statement:
\begin{theorem}[the three $I_1^*$ profiles give no natural sphere]\label{maps:src:D.2.27}



None of the natural section-line inputs on
\[
 (I_1^*,I_3,I_1,I_1),\qquad (I_1^*,II,I_3),\qquad
 (I_1^*,IV,I_1)
\]
produces a homotopy six-sphere, for any permitted original,
logarithmic or Mumford filling, multiplicity or affine twist in
the sector of \ref{maps:src:D.2.22}. The obstruction is integral. In the only
remaining minimal star caps, the full normal-kernel indices are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
 m_*&\text{component action}&H_2(U_*;\mathbb Z)
       &\kappa_*\ \text{(normal projection index)}\\\hline
 2&\text{one component}&\mathbb Z^2&1\\
 4&\text{two components interchanged}&
                   \mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Z/2&4.
\end{array}                                                   \tag{D.ST1}\label{maps:eq:D.ST1}
\]
If the complete output is simply connected and its other caps
have the minimal rational ranks, the order of $H_2$ has exactly
one factor of $2$ in the first row, and exactly two factors of $2$
in the second row. In particular $H_2\ne0$.

\end{theorem}

statement:
\begin{theorem}[a corrected compact construction]\label{maps:src:E.1.2}



There is a smooth compact complex fourfold $Z$ with proper holomorphic
maps $g:Z\to B$ and $\Pi:Z\to X$, with $g=f\Pi$, satisfying the local
models and the marked punctured-fibre product specified here.  The map $\Pi$
has a holomorphic section.  The construction is a small crepant
resolution of a Weierstrass model over $X$, and is bimeromorphic to
$X\times_B S$.

\end{theorem}

statement:
\begin{theorem}[fundamental group and rational homology]\label{maps:src:E.1.4}



The fourfold in Theorem \ref{maps:src:E.1.2} has
\[
 \pi_1(Z)=1,\qquad \chi(Z)=6,\qquad
 (b_0,\ldots,b_8)=(1,0,2,1,2,1,2,0,1).
 \tag{E.8}\label{maps:eq:E.8}

The first homology groups of its two finite reduced fibres are,
respectively, $\mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Z/3$ and
$\mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Z/2$.

\end{theorem}

label: maps:src:B.6.17
statement:
\begin{proposition}[the actual quotient Pontryagin class]\label{maps:src:B.6.17}


Retain the reference cusp fan fixed in the construction of this
family, with its specified lattice basis and collar maps.



Use the fixed-circle replacement of \ref{maps:src:B.6.16}, the positive parameter
loop, and the mapping-torus convention
$(z,1)\sim(\Phi z,0)$ of \ref{maps:src:B.6.1}.  Let $M_s$ be its
seven-dimensional mapping torus and let
\[
 \pi:M_s\longrightarrow Q=M_s/S^1_\delta
\]
be the principal circle bundle, with Euler class $x$.
Orient $Q$ by putting the positive $\delta$ direction first
in the orientation of $M_s$.  The bundle over the parameter
circle has fibre $S^2\times S^3$.  The class $x$ is primitive,
and there is a unique $y\in H^4(Q;\mathbb Z)$ with
$\langle xy,[Q]\rangle=1$.  If $Z_1,Z_2\subset Q$ are the
quotients of the two swept critical elliptic curves, oriented
by their complex normal bundles, then
\[
 p_1(Q)=-2\operatorname{PD}_Q(Z_1+Z_2),\qquad
 \langle x,[Z_1]\rangle=2,\quad
 \langle x,[Z_2]\rangle=0.
 \tag{B.Q1}\label{maps:eq:B.Q1}
\]
Consequently
\[
                       p_1(Q)=-4y.
 \tag{B.Q2}\label{maps:eq:B.Q2}
\]
This computes the integer $\ell$ in \ref{maps:src:B.6.15}, with these
orientations.  It does not compute $k$ in $x^2=ky$ or the
relative Pontryagin number of the parametrized surgery trace.

\end{proposition}

label: maps:src:B.6.20
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{maps:src:B.6.20}


Retain the reference cusp fan fixed in the construction of this
family, with its specified lattice basis and collar maps.



For the marked fixed-curve surgery of the minimal $(3,4)$ family in
\ref{maps:src:B.6.16}, let $Q$ be the six-dimensional free-circle quotient of the
parameter mapping torus. Its primitive Euler class $e$ satisfies
$|\langle e^3,[Q]\rangle|=1$. In the oriented convention of \ref{maps:src:B.6.17},
$\ell=-4$, hence the spin congruence of \ref{maps:src:B.6.15} gives $k=-1$.

\end{theorem}

label: night:P3K.9
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{night:P3K.9}

For the rotating framing specified below, the one-gamma-turn
return has meridian-line Jin numbers
\((k_U,\ell_U)=(-6,-24)\) and physical-line numbers
\((k_M,\ell_M)=(6,24)\), where \(U=M^{-1}\).
After removing an extending constant-rotation loop, this framing
descends through the sixfold parameter cover.  With the descended
framing the original positive return has

\[
 (k_U,\ell_U)=(-1,-4),\qquad (k_M,\ell_M)=(1,4).
\]

Every other tubular framing differs by the explicitly described
changes \((k,\ell)\mapsto(k+n,\ell+4n)\) of P3F.11.  The asserted
individual values include the framing; their index is independent
of that choice.
\end{theorem}

label: night:P3K.11
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{night:P3K.11}

Fix logarithmic orders \(3K,4L\), with
\(\gcd(3K,4L)=1\), and primitive logarithmic coefficients
\(n_0,n_1\), so \(\gcd(n_0,3K)=\gcd(n_1,4L)=1\).
For the sphere members impose
\(a=4L n_0+3K n_1=\pm1\), with zero additional cusp collar.
Use the period coordinate \(c\) and scalar \(u\) of the original
family.  The closed higher parameter is
\[
 w_h=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi i c}{KL}\right),
 \qquad u=\kappa w_h^{2KL},\qquad \kappa\ne0.
\]
In particular, the original expression \(w=\exp(-\pi i c)\)
does not give one closed higher loop when \(KL>1\).
The positive sixfold cover \(w_h=r^6\) gives the signed
gamma turn \(a\gamma\).  For the positive-gamma sphere marking
\(a=1\), with the descended rotating framing of P3K.9, the Jin
integers of the positive \(w_h\)-loop are
\[
 (k_U,\ell_U)=(-KL,-4KL),\qquad
 (k_M,\ell_M)=(KL,4KL).
\]
The integer return index is zero for either sphere sign.
These statements identify
both the parameter and the framing in the supplied higher-order
formulas.
\end{theorem}

label: maps:src:F.3.6
statement:
\begin{theorem}[a global nonpolarized period family]\label{maps:src:F.3.6}



The integral rank-six system with cohomology monodromies $A,B$
admits a holomorphic subbundle $\mathcal F$ of rank three over
$U$ satisfying $\mathcal F\cap\overline{\mathcal F}=0$.
It extends holomorphically on the finite root charts.  At the
cusp an integral marking puts its periods in the form
\[
 Z(t)=\frac{\log t}{2\pi i}I_3+C(t),
 \tag{F.13}\label{maps:eq:F.13}
\]
where $C$ is holomorphic at zero and bounded there.

\end{theorem}

label: cdp:st:C.2.INT.3
statement:
\begin{proposition}[Proved sign and equality for every reducible fibre]\label{cdp:st:C.2.INT.3}



Let $f:Y\to B$ satisfy the hypotheses of \ref{cdp:st:C.2.INT.2},
and let $S$ be a connected reducible fibre support.
Then
\[
 e(S)\ge0.
 \tag{C.INT.15}\label{cdp:eq:C.INT.15}
\]
Equality holds precisely when the normalization of $S$
is a disjoint union of smooth minimal Hopf or
non-K\"ahler elliptic surfaces, and the reduced
conductor image and its reduced inverse image are
disjoint unions of smooth elliptic curves. The maps
between these elliptic curves are finite unramified
covers. This criterion allows arbitrary conductor
scheme structure and arbitrary unequal multiplicities
of the full fibre.
\end{proposition}
